title: Sphere HTML time series are stride-decimated twice, and JS KPIs (peak G, pulse, crack arrest, hotspot element) are computed from what is left
mechanism: loader.py:727-735 load_target = report_pts*4 (400/120/60/40), then loader.py:267-273 `ts.times = all_t[::step]` / 316-319 motion `buf[k][::step]`. Next, html_report.py:140 `ts_pts = 100 if n_results <= 50 else 30 ... else 10` and 194/205/213 `step = max(1, len(pr.stress.times) // ts_pts)` plus `range(0, len, step)` stride again. true_peak is kept only for the scalar peak_* fields. The JS then recomputes peaks from these series: 3366 `const peakG = Math.max(...gvals.map(Math.abs))` (Impact Phase Timing 'Peak G'/'Time to Peak'), 4011 `absMax` in computePulseMetrics (Impact Pulse 'Max Peak (MG)', pulse width, impulse, half-sine), 4369 detectPeaks (Rebound), 4551 `const peakStress = Math.max(...sMax)` (Crack Arrest CAI), and 3447-3448/4156-4157 `eid = elems[maxIdx]` (hot-spot / critical element tables). Time History charts (2716-2734) plot the same decimated series.
scenario: Real production campaign /data/Tests/Test_006_Fibonacci_6deg (1144 runs, 992 states per run). Loader keeps 42 points and HTML keeps 11. I ran the snapshot's loader and stride on 240 motion series from 40 runs. Median g_ts peak is 39% of the true peak_g. Worst case: Run_20260207_225111_ac4ff7 part 10, true 139,029 G vs 16,928 G in g_ts (12%). For stress, median is 85% of true and worst is Run_20260207_215839_edb467 part 14, 227.6 MPa true vs 61.5 MPa (27%). In the <=200-run tier (where stress_ts.elem is emitted), 12 of 68 real stress series put the hotspot element on a different element than the true-peak element (e.g. part 11: true peak elem 34016 at 62.83 MPa, report elem 34022 at 56.01 MPa).
consumers: koo_sphere_report report.html: Impact Analysis tab (phase timing table and scatter, hot-spot element table), Advanced tab (Impact Pulse KPIs/table, Critical Element, Rebound, Crack Arrest CAI), Part Deep Dive time-domain section, Time History charts. The same decimated stress_ts/g_ts also goes into report.json (json_report.py:111-133).
suggested_fix: Decimate with peak preservation (per-bucket min/max, always including the true-peak and true-min indices), or compute the pulse, CAI and hotspot-element metrics in Python on full-resolution data and embed only the scalars. Do not stride twice: size the loader target to the final ts_pts, or have the HTML reuse the loader series without restriding.

title: σ3 minimum, ε3 minimum and peak_vel come from loader-decimated series (no true-min is captured)
mechanism: loader.py:261-265 records only `ts.true_peak = all_max[peak_idx]` before `ts.min_values = all_min[::step]`. models.py:235-241 `min_principal`: `vals = list(ts.min_values or []) ...; return min(vals)`. min_principal_strain (225-232) does the same. html_report.py:237 `pd['peak_vel'] = round(max(abs(v) for v in pr.motion.avg_vel_mag) ...)` also runs on the decimated avg_vel_mag.
scenario: I fed a 992-state part_7_min_principal_stress.csv with Min=-30 MPa everywhere except a -412 MPa compressive spike at state 437 to the snapshot `_load_stress_strain_csv`. min_principal returns -30.0 for every tier (target 40, 120 and 400; 992//400=2 still skips odd index 437). The true value is -412.0.
consumers: report.json `min_principal_stress` / `min_principal_strain` (json_report.py:89-96) feed koo_federate_report sphere adapter metrics s3/e3. HTML payload (html_report.py:175-180) feeds the Part Risk σ3/ε3 columns, the Mollweide/heatmap σ3 quantity and the Tolerance DOE tab. peak_vel feeds the heatmap, correlation matrix and deep-dive worst velocity.
suggested_fix: In _load_stress_strain_csv, also capture true_min/true_min_time over all_min before decimation (and true peak |vel| in _load_motion_csv). Make min_principal / min_principal_strain / peak_vel use them.

title: Sphere HTML payload rounds stress/strain/disp to 1-2 / 4-6 decimals, so GPa stresses and small strains collapse
mechanism: `s_prec = 1 if n_results > 500 else 2`, `e_prec = 4 if n_results > 500 else 6`, `t_prec = 6 if ... else 7`, applied at 166-182 (`round(pr.peak_stress, s_prec)`, `round(pr.peak_strain, e_prec)`, `round(pr.peak_disp, s_prec)`, `round(pr.min_principal, s_prec)`) and to every stress_ts/strain_ts/disp_ts sample (196-235). Display adds more loss: formatValue 2163 `v.toFixed(1) + ' MPa'`, 2168 `(v/1e6).toFixed(2) + ' MG'`. Tolerance tab 5702 `if (v == null || !isFinite(v) || v === 0) continue;` treats a rounded 0 as missing.
scenario: Snapshot _build_report_data with a GPa deck (kg-mm-ms) and 7 angles with true peak_stress 0.0863 to 0.0915. All 7 become 0.09 at 26 runs and 0.1 at 1144 runs (one distinct value, so risk ranking and Mollweide contour go flat). σ3 -0.0042 becomes -0.0 and stress_ts.avg 0.004 becomes 0.0, so the energy absorption integral (4262-4276) is 0 and the section disappears. With 1144 runs (the production Fibonacci size) an MPa deck with eff. plastic strain 4.2e-5 gives peak_strain 0.0, which the guide text says means 'purely elastic'. The Tolerance tab then drops that case as if no value existed and reports '정각도(_NOM) 없음'. In an SI deck, displacement 0.0123 m becomes 0.01 (<=500 runs) or 0.0 (>500 runs).
consumers: Every sphere HTML tab that reads pd.peak_* or *_ts: Mollweide map and risk table, Part Risk, Heatmap, Statistics, Failure SF (safety_factor returns 0/'N/A' when peak_stress rounds to 0), Tolerance DOE sensitivity, Energy Absorption, Crack Arrest.
suggested_fix: Round to significant figures, not fixed decimals (e.g. float(f'{v:.4g}')), or skip rounding and let gzip/JSON size tiers handle payload. In JS, format with toPrecision/exponential and stop treating 0 as missing in tolAngleValue.

title: Federate takes max() for σ3/ε3 (negative, compressive), so the 'worst' is the least-compressive value and deltas invert
mechanism: sphere.py:93 cell aggregation `if v is not None and (agg[mk] is None or v > agg[mk])` runs for all metrics including s3/e3 (the impact adapter uses METRIC_COMPRESSIVE here). compare.py also uses max for part worst (493 `if best_v is None or v > best_v`), rank (559-564 `reverse=True`), true peak (744), worst_per_rev (769, 784) and category worst (167 `max(vals)`); tiers.py:117 anchor uses `v > best_v`. Only the per-cell winner (400) honours METRIC_COMPRESSIVE. compare.py:324-326 also raises a severity ERROR 'negative_metric' for any negative s3/e3.
scenario: Ran the snapshot adapters and compare with metric='s3'. Sidecar A has PCB σ3 = -350/-349/-348 and FOAM σ3 = -0.4 at 3 angles; B has PCB -500.. and FOAM -0.3. Output: cell s3 is [-0.4,-0.4,-0.4] vs [-0.3,...]; true_peak_per_rev [-0.4, -0.3] (shown as +25% improvement while the real worst went -350 to -500, 43% worse); FOAM ranked 1 (worst) and PCB ranked 2; PCB worst [-348, -498] instead of [-350, -500]; warnings ['negative_metric','negative_metric'] as ERROR on valid data.
consumers: koo_federate_report CLI `--metric s3|e3`: KPI table (참피크/WORST), parts trend and rank-bump table, category summary bars, profile anchor selection, console summary and payload JSON.
suggested_fix: Use one helper, worse(v, cur, metric) = v < cur for METRIC_COMPRESSIVE, else v > cur, in the sphere adapter aggregation, compare part worst / true peak / worst_per_rev / category worst / rank sort, and tiers anchor. Exclude s3/e3 from the negative_metric guard.

title: Federate HTML divides every metric by the acceleration G divisor and prints 0 decimals, so stress and strain show as '0'
mechanism: compare.py:843 `g_divisor = 9.81 if _acc in (...) else (9810.0 if _acc == 'mm/s²' else None)` is set from unit_labels.acc regardless of `metric`. JS 1199 `var GDIV = ...DATA.g_divisor`, 1201 `var VUNIT = GDIV ? 'G' : ...`, 1209 `function gv(v) { return isN(v) ? (GDIV ? v / GDIV : v) : null; }`, used in 1276 profVal, 1717 bars, 1740 `fnum(gv(pr.value), 0)`, 1744 Δ, 1849 part worst `fnum(gv(w[i]), 0)`. The Python category summary and KPI table also use `_num(v / div, 0)`.
scenario: Snapshot run with two impact sidecars (unit_labels.acc 'mm/s²') and `--metric s`: payload g_divisor = 9810.0. The probe VALUE cell for 470 MPa renders fnum(470/9810, 0) = '0' under header 'VALUE (G)', and Δ 50 MPa also shows '0'. Sphere sidecar (GDIV=0) with `--metric e` and strain 0.0021 renders '0' in the probe, part-trend table and category bars; only Δ% survives.
consumers: Federate report sections: profile tooltip/axis label, probe bar chart and table, parts trend table, category summary bars, KPI table for GPa stresses.
suggested_fix: Apply g_divisor only when DATA.metric === 'g' (and send the metric's own unit label). Choose decimals by magnitude (toPrecision(4) or exponent for |v|<1).

title: Scatter direction map fixes pitch axis to ±90° while production DOEs use pitch ±180°, so about 40% of runs are drawn outside the SVG
mechanism: `grid, px, py = _axes(w, h, pad, -180, 180, -90, 90, "roll [deg]", "pitch [deg]", 6, 4)`. py() does not clip (`_norm` is unbounded), so points with |pitch|>~95 land outside viewBox 0..380 and are clipped by the browser. lo/hi for the colour bar still include them. The caller is report/html_report.py:94 `C.direction_map([(v[4], v[5], v[3]) ...])` with raw DropSet roll/pitch.
scenario: Real campaign /data/Tests/Test_006_Fibonacci_6deg: DropSet roll ∈ [-86.6, 84.1], pitch ∈ [-178.5, 177.5]. 572 of 1144 runs have |pitch|>90 and 465 are fully outside the viewBox. Snapshot direction_map([(-40,30,100),(-40,150,480),(20,-170,350)]) puts the 480-valued (worst) point at cy=-94.0 and the 350 point at cy=492.7, both invisible. The colour bar still reads max 480.
consumers: koo_scatter_report HTML section '② 방향도 (roll–pitch)', meant to show 'which posture is dangerous'.
suggested_fix: Use the convention the sphere loader auto-detects (lat=roll ±90, lon=pitch ±180, swapped when max|roll|>91), or derive axis ranges from the data. Clip or flag out-of-range points instead of drawing them off-canvas.

title: report.json (federate sidecar) rounds peak stress to 2 decimals, strain to 6 and disp to 3; series stress_ts to 1 decimal
scenario: Snapshot save_json with a GPa deck: peak_stress 0.0863 becomes 0.09; σ3 -0.0042 becomes -0.0; stress_ts.max 0.0915 becomes 0.1; eff. plastic strain 4.2e-7 becomes 0.0. Two revisions with true peak stress 0.0863 GPa and 0.0891 GPa (+3.2%) both write 0.09, so koo_federate_report shows Δ 0.0%. An SI-deck displacement of 0.0004 m is written as 0.0 and federate _pct(new, 0) returns None.
consumers: koo_federate_report adapters/sphere.py (_METRIC_SRC s,e,d,s1,s3,e1,e3,evm), which drives every federate Δ/trend/rank. Also --from-json regeneration (from_json.py) and any external reader of report.json.
suggested_fix: Write full-precision floats (or significant-figure rounding such as float(f'{v:.6g}')) for scalar peaks. If size matters, only the time-series arrays need compacting.

title: Missing stress/strain/motion CSV is reported as a measured 0 (peak_stress/peak_strain/peak_g/peak_disp)
mechanism: `def peak_stress(self): return self.stress.peak if self.stress else 0.0` (208); likewise peak_strain 245, peak_g 249, peak_disp 253. loader.py:422-452 leaves pr.stress/strain/motion None when the CSV does not exist, and unified_analyzer.cpp exportResults writes motion CSVs only for parts in motion_analysis. json_report.py:76-79 and html_report.py:166-169 serialize the 0.0. federate adapters/sphere.py:90 `_num(0.0)` keeps it as a real value.
scenario: The shipped example python/koo_sphere_report/examples/Test_001_report.json has parts 1 and 2 with peak_stress 461.2 but peak_strain 0.0, peak_g 0.0, peak_disp 0.0 (no motion/strain CSV). In federate, a part that has motion in revision A (150,000 G) but not in B reports worst [150000, 0.0], Δ% -100% ('improved'), data_status 'ok'; the no_metric path never fires. In the sphere HTML the guide says a strain of 0 means 'purely elastic'.
consumers: Sphere HTML (Mollweide, risk table, Part Risk, Statistics, correlation matrix), analyzer findings, report.json, then federate part trends/ranks/Δ and KPI n_parts_no_metric.
suggested_fix: Return None when the series is absent (as peak_principal already does), omit the key in json_report/html payload, and let JS/federate show '—' / no_metric.

title: Sphere resample pairs cells by index-based angle name (P0200) as 'exact measured' even when the directions differ by up to 102°
mechanism: nearest mode: `exact = next((c for c in b.cells if c.key == cell.key), None)` then `_sample_from_cell(exact, "exact", True, 0.0)`. off mode 333 `common = set.intersection(*keysets)` joins by key; identity 306-318 also keys by name. Real Fibonacci DOE names are P0001..P1146 by index (runner_config.json of Test_006), so the same name means a different direction on a different-size grid.
scenario: Snapshot align() on sphere sidecars from Fibonacci N=1144 (6°) and N=412 (10°), both named P%04d. nearest: 412 cells marked exact/measured, the worst pair P0412 at (16.3°, -4.3°) vs (-86.0°, -4.3°), 102.3° apart with offset 0.0. off: 'measured_pct': 100.0, 'coverage_pct': 100.0, same 102° pairs.
consumers: Federate Δ/trend/winner maps, profile, probe, part trends, KPI measured_pct (the '실측률' headline) and the no_measured_cells warning.
suggested_fix: For sphere, define an 'exact' match by angular distance (<= _ANGLE_EXACT_DEG between roll/pitch/yaw vectors), not by name. At minimum, verify that name-matched cells are within tolerance and warn or demote otherwise.

title: IDW resample interpolates only g/s/e/d, so s1/s3/e1/e3/evm become None and every interpolated cell is gated as '값 없음'
mechanism: `for mk in ("g", "s", "e", "d"):` builds Sample.metrics; the other METRIC_KEYS are absent, so compare.scaled returns None, `complete=False`, and gate reason is `"값 없음: " + label`.
scenario: Snapshot run: two sphere sidecars with 100 Fibonacci angles, B offset by 3° pitch, every cell carrying peak_principal_stress 250. `resample: idw` gives metric s n_comparable 100/100 but metric s1 n_comparable 0/100 with gate_reason '값 없음: B', although B has s1 at every angle.
consumers: Federate report with options.resample: idw and --metric s1|s3|e1|e3|evm: all Δ maps, profile, parts table (gated) and no_comparable_cells ERROR blaming the data.
suggested_fix: Iterate over models.METRIC_KEYS in _idw_sample. For compressive metrics interpolate the signed value; do not report interpolation gaps as '값 없음'.

title: --from-json regeneration fabricates 2-point waveforms, drops σ1/σ3/ε/energy, and uses the stress peak time for strain
mechanism: `_make_stress_ts`: `times=[0.0, peak_time], max_values=[0.0, peak], avg_values=[0.0, peak]`; `_make_motion`: `mo.avg_acc_mag = [0.0, gval]` with `t = peak_g_time if peak_g_time > 0 else 0.001`. 174-177 strain uses `pd.get("time_of_peak_stress", 0.001)`. peak_principal_stress, min_principal_stress, *_strain, energy, stress_ts/g_ts and tool_builds in report.json are never read.
scenario: Snapshot round trip: report.json keys include min_principal_stress, peak_principal_stress, energy, stress_ts, g_ts. The regenerated payload has none of the principal/energy keys. stress_ts becomes {'t': [0.0, 0.00037], 'max': [0.0, 300.0], 'avg': [0.0, 300.0]} (avg = peak is invented) and g_ts becomes {'t': [0.0, 0.0003], 'g': [0.0, 5096.8]}. Strain peak_time is 0.00037 instead of 0.00151. Time History draws a straight ramp, Impact Pulse computes width/impulse from 2 points, Crack Arrest SCF becomes 1.0, and σ1/σ3 columns disappear.
consumers: koo_sphere_report CLI `--from-json` → report.html (all time-series tabs, Part Risk principal/energy columns, build note).
suggested_fix: Load the stored stress_ts/strain_ts/g_ts/disp_ts, principal, strain and energy keys. If a series is absent, leave it empty and hide the dependent sections instead of synthesizing [0, peak]. Use each quantity's own peak time.

title: Sphere unit detection maps every ms-based deck to ton-mm-s (or keeps it as default), so peak G is 1e6× too small
mechanism: `preset = _detect_unit_system(density)`; `gf = _G_FACTOR_BY_UNIT.get(uid)`; if uid is unknown it keeps `MotionData.G_FACTOR = 9810`. koo_impact_report/loader.py:1011 `if density <= 1.0e-5: return _UNIT_PRESETS["ton-mm-s"]` and 1016 `return _UNIT_UNKNOWN`, so the 'ton-mm-ms'/'g-mm-ms' entries in _G_FACTOR_BY_UNIT (88-89) can never be selected. The only signal is a stdout print.
scenario: Snapshot detector: ton-mm-ms steel ρ=7.85e-9 is detected as 'ton-mm-s' (G_FACTOR 9806.65); kg-mm-ms ρ=7.85e-6 is also 'ton-mm-s'; g-mm-ms ρ=7.85e-3 is '' and falls back to 9810. A true 150,000 G peak (acc in mm/ms²) is reported as 0.15 G. The HTML shows 0.00 MG and analyzer's `worst_g > 50000` finding never fires.
consumers: peak_g/true_peak_g, g_ts/acc_ts in HTML and report.json, analyzer CRITICAL/WARNING G findings, federate metric g.
suggested_fix: Disambiguate time/mass units with more than density (e.g. analysis_result.json end_time magnitude or the deck's *CONTROL_TERMINATION, impact velocity from drop height). When undetermined, mark peak_g as unit-unknown in the payload and HTML instead of silently applying 9810.

title: Sphere sidecars get hard-coded MPa/mm/G unit labels, so the federate unit-mismatch guard can never fire for sphere revisions
mechanism: `unit_labels=dict(raw.get("unit_labels") or _SPHERE_DEFAULT_UNITS)` where `_SPHERE_DEFAULT_UNITS = {"acc": "G", "stress": "MPa", "disp": "mm", ...}` (31-40). json_report.py never writes unit_labels or the detected unit system. compare.py:_unit_factors (234-236) sees identical labels and returns factor 1.0 with no warning, even under unit_policy 'error'.
scenario: Revision A from an SI deck (stress Pa: peak 3.1e8, disp m: 0.012) vs revision B from a ton-mm-s deck (310 MPa, 12 mm). Both are labeled MPa/mm, so federate reports stress Δ% = -99.9999% and disp Δ% = -99.9% as real improvements with no unit_converted/unit_unknown warning.
consumers: Federate Δ/trend/winner/parts for metrics s, s1, s3, d (and e unaffected); KPI table unit captions.
suggested_fix: Have koo_sphere_report json_report write unit_labels from the detected unit system (MotionData.UNIT_SYSTEM plus the impact presets). In the adapter, leave labels empty when absent so the guard can warn about unknown units instead of inventing MPa/mm.
